mission: Shift lipid mediator balance from pro-inflammatory eicosanoids toward pro-resolving signals that terminate inflammation.

stage2a.operation: Precursor substrate capacity retained; mediator formation and clinical termination of inflammation remain distinct. EPA/DHA are Direct to the owned biosynthetic operation, not direct food sources of SPMs.

existing_findings.proposition: EPA and DHA are the fatty-acid substrates for resolvins and protectins. Those mediators support resolution of inflammation rather than only blocking it.

existing_source_assessments.label: Serhan and Petasis (2011)
existing_source_assessments.exposure_context: review of resolvin and protectin biosynthesis
existing_source_assessments.directional_finding: Resolvins and protectins are generated from EPA and DHA and act in resolution, distinct from inflammatory blockade.

assessment.study: Chemical review of resolvins and protectins.
assessment.population: Biosynthetic and cell literature. No new human feeding trial.
assessment.result: EPA and DHA are the precursors of these pro-resolving mediators.
assessment.evidence_summary: The substrates of this balance are EPA and DHA.
assessment.limitations: Substrate identity is not a clinical resolution result.

existing_supportive_evidence.label: Simopoulos (2011)
existing_supportive_evidence.why_relevant: Reviews competition between omega-6 and omega-3 fatty acids in mediator pathways.
existing_supportive_evidence.why_excluded: An evolutionary ratio review is not the identification of resolvins and not a measurement of mediators after intake.

existing_findings.disposition: Existing canonical assessment retained; enrichment is additive. No clinical or source-level negative inferred from bounded retrieval.

existing_findings.proposition: Five days of 2.4 g a day of n-3 fatty acids raised selected pro-resolving mediators in healthy adults. Not every mediator rose, and aspirin added no further increase.

existing_source_assessments.label: Barden et al. (2014)
existing_source_assessments.exposure_context: 2.4 g/day n-3 fatty acids for 5–7 days
existing_source_assessments.directional_finding: RvE1, 18-HEPE, 17-HDHA, and 14-HDHA rose. Other specialised pro-resolving mediators did not. Aspirin added no further rise.

assessment.study: Open supplementation of n-3 fatty acids for seven days, with random aspirin or placebo from day 5 to day 7.
assessment.result: Selected E-series and pathway markers rose by day 5. MaR1 stayed below detection. Aspirin did not change the mediators.
assessment.effect_magnitude: The paper reports a significant rise in RvE1, 18-HEPE, 17-HDHA, and 14-HDHA, and no rise in the other measured specialised pro-resolving mediators.
assessment.evidence_summary: A short n-3 intake can raise some circulating pro-resolving mediators.
assessment.limitations: This is not every mediator, not a disease population, and not proof that inflammation resolved.

existing_findings.disposition: Existing canonical assessment retained; enrichment is additive. No clinical or source-level negative inferred from bounded retrieval.

stage2a.evidence_enrichment: The human n-3 exposure changed selected mediator concentrations, with important null or undetected analytes. Concentrations, biosynthetic flux, inflammatory resolution and clinical brain outcomes are not interchangeable.

source_to_claim_records.proposition: Selected plasma n-3 pathway mediators changed during combined n-3 supplementation.
source_to_claim_records.limitation: Not all mediators increased; aspirin randomisation is distinct from uncontrolled pre/post n-3 exposure; no demonstrated clinical resolution or fish-meal equivalence.
source_to_claim_records.retrieval: Primary full text, Table 2 and design.

stage2a.coverage_limitations: Existing source assessments and full attached bibliography are inventoried and preserved. Targeted source retrieval is bounded to the stated propositions; unrefreshed clinical/Phenome sources are not newly validated. No evidence of absence is inferred.
stage2a.stop_rationale: Preserve the complete baseline, add the bounded supported evidence and exact qualifications, and park material attribution/traceability questions for approval instead of forcing an admission or expanding to a comprehensive rebuild.

preserved_phenome_source_records.rationale: Specialized pro-resolving mediators actively terminate inflammation without suppressing immune surveillance — supporting cognitive clarity context through resolution-oriented lipid signalling.
Omega-3-derived resolution biology may modulate affective inflammatory context when EPA/DHA substrate and omega-6:omega-3 balance are adequate over habitual intake.
Resolution-phase lipid mediator balance may intersect attention-relevant inflammatory tone; direct ADHD SPM outcome evidence remains limited.

Persistent inflammatory signalling and impaired resolution-phase lipid mediator balance are recognised contributors to anxious perseverative cognition within neuroimmune framing (Slavich & Irwin, 2014; Marsland et al., 2017). SPM-oriented resolution biology and human omega-3 intervention reduced inflammatory markers and anxiety symptoms alongside cytokine remodelling (Kiecolt-Glaser et al., 2011; Ferguson et al., 2014). This PM governs eicosanoid–SPM balance — not omega-3 treatment — and attached anxiety outcomes require one inferential step to PH016 rather than direct perseverative-thought measurement.

Resolution-phase eicosanoid balance may modulate inflammatory tone intersecting reward-processing and depressive biology in translational framing; Gruber et al. (2023) reviews insulin–dopamine reward disruption in depression as adjacent context.
